name: Aarchid — AI Botanical Intelligence
tagline: Photograph a sick plant, get a diagnosis you can act on.
decision: Require a source link on every recommendation, and judge prompt changes against a fixed golden set, not by feel.
description: Photograph a sick plant and get a diagnosis you can act on. Multimodal vision grounded by research-augmented LLM reasoning instead of a confident guess. Co-built with Dilpreet Grover: I owned product, evaluation and orchestration.
imageAlt: Aarchid landing page showing the AI plant diagnosis interface and digital twin positioning.
metricLabel: A source link required on every recommendation · offline eval result withheld; field accuracy not measured
ownership: Co-built with Dilpreet Grover · product, eval, orchestration
evidenceNote: Self-reported: the team ran an offline eval on a golden set. The result is withheld here until the eval artefact or the co-builder's confirmation is available.

name: DeskTasks — Desktop Task Widget
tagline: Your task list, pinned behind every window on the desktop.
decision: Pin the widget behind every window, not on top of them, and refuse attention: accountless, local-first, no dock icon.
statusNote: Hosted v1.3.1 line is frozen; v2 alpha runs locally
description: Puts the task list on the desktop itself, pinned behind every window instead of buried in another tab. Natural-language quick-add, recurring tasks, reminders, time tracking, and .ics/CSV/Markdown round-trips. Two release lines: hosted v1.3.x with Supabase sync (frozen Sept 2026) and a local v2.0.0-alpha line with local hub sync.
imageAlt: Three DeskTasks widget panels on a dark ground: the pinned task list, natural-language quick-add parsing a date, time and tag, and a filtered search.
duration: 2026 · v1.3.x frozen Sept 2026, v2.0.0-alpha in progress

name: Cohort & Retention Studio: D2C Retention in the Browser
tagline: Cohort retention for D2C order exports, computed in your browser.
decision: Compute every metric in the browser, in a Web Worker: raw order rows never leave the tab, and only aggregates can be saved.
description: Drop an orders CSV and get cohort retention curves, repeat rate, time to second order, LTV by first product and a free-shipping what-if. Raw order rows never leave the browser: every metric is computed in a Web Worker, and only finished aggregates can be saved. Ready for a facilitated local pilot; the hosted product has not been verified.
metricLabel: E2E tests passing (19 Sep 2026) · local pilot ready
ownership: Solo · product, metric definitions and engineering

name: Sawari: Auto-Rickshaw Sharing
tagline: Share the auto you booked; split the fare by kilometres ridden.
decision: Riders only, driver out of the loop: post-and-join ride sharing, with the owner approving each joiner.
audience: Auto-rickshaw commuters in Mumbai and Bangalore
description: Rider-to-rider auto-rickshaw sharing: one rider posts the auto they booked, riders whose route it covers ask to join, and the owner approves each joiner. Drivers are not users, so there is no two-sided marketplace. The fare is split by the kilometres each rider shared. Built on Elixir, Phoenix LiveView and Ash. Locally built and tested, not deployed.
metricLabel: Tests passing · local build, not deployed

name: ExperimentHub — A/B Testing Platform
tagline: Self-hosted A/B testing with deterministic variant assignment.
decision: Let the statistics engine say no: return a sequential verdict such as keep running, not a bare p-value.
businessModel: Self-hosted · public repo, no licence file yet
description: Self-hosted A/B testing whose statistics engine is allowed to say keep running: a sequential verdict instead of a bare p-value, and assignment that puts the same user in the same variant every time. Built solo; evidence so far is a synthetic demo tenant, not production use.
imageAlt: ExperimentHub command centre on the synthetic demo tenant: running experiments, draft queue, assignments today, enabled flags, recent experiments and a lifecycle snapshot.
imageCaption: Command centre on the demo tenant; every number is synthetic seed data.

name: KiteEdge — Personal Analytics Desk
tagline: A personal portfolio-analytics desk for one Zerodha account.
decision: Analytics only: the tool reads the Kite account and never writes to it, so there is no order placement.
description: A personal analytics desk for my own Zerodha account, running on my own laptop: technical indicators, Monte Carlo VaR, ensemble forecasting, a NIFTY 500 screener and a FIFO trade journal. Private by design; the tests run on synthetic data only.
imageAlt: QuantStats tear sheet from KiteEdge's report module, rendered on seeded synthetic returns, not account data.
imageCaption: Tear sheet rendered on seeded synthetic returns, not account data.
metricLabel: Never places an order · synthetic data in tests
ownership: Solo · personal tool, product and architecture

name: TCS NQT Prep Hub
tagline: Free, offline-capable TCS NQT prep with 404 practice questions.
decision: Offline-first before anything else: cache the app shell and question bank on first load so it works with the network off.
description: Built so a candidate can prepare for the TCS NQT without a paid prep course: 404 practice questions and 10 previous papers (counts per the repo README), quizzes, flashcards and progress tracking. Installable as a PWA and usable offline.
imageAlt: TCS NQT Prep Hub dashboard showing topic progress, recent activity, and study metrics.
ownership: Built the web app · question bank started by three other contributors
team: Web app: solo. Question bank: three other contributors.

name: Hackmate — Co-Founder Matchmaking Platform
tagline: Find the co-founder you'd actually build with.
decision: Optimise for speed to first match: keep onboarding and profile setup light so a new user reaches profiles quickly.
description: Designed to help solo founders find a co-founder they would actually build with: swipe-based matching shaped around founder-discovery pain points. A two-person build; usage was never instrumented, so there is no user number to report.

name: Better-Half — Cycle-Aware Companion
tagline: Cycle-aware daily guidance for long-distance couples.
decision: Enforce consent in the database, not the interface: every sharing choice maps to a row-level security policy.
description: Helps a long-distance couple stay in sync when they can't read the room in person. Cycle phase, mood and stress drive daily guidance for her, him and us. Private, used by two people. Privacy is enforced at the database rather than the UI: 575 RLS policy checks, offline-first, hosted on free tiers ($0 a month, self-recorded).
imageAlt: Illustrative mock-up with invented demo data: Person A's view with a cycle estimate, check-in, sharing dials and a suggestion; Person B's view with his own state, guidance, only the categories Person A shared, and a weekly retro.
imageCaption: Illustrative mock-up with invented demo data, not the private deployment.

name: This Portfolio — Meta Case Study
tagline: A portfolio treated as a product, decision trail included.
decision: Treat case studies as content, not pages: one MDX file per study, so adding or correcting one is a one-file change.
description: Treated my own portfolio as a product: spec and success criteria before code, then versioned iterations from v1 (Jan 2026) to v6 (Sept 2026), with the decision trail written up as its own case study.
imageAlt: Portfolio home page: the headline about owning the problem, the spec, the trade-offs and the evidence, a contents list, and the first featured case studies.

name: Weekly Retro — Relationship Performance Review
tagline: Corporate performance-review theatre, applied to a relationship, on purpose.
description: Corporate performance-review theatre, applied to a relationship, entirely on purpose: log a week of small signals and a scoring engine assembles a shareable 12-slide review deck, trajectory and areas of assessment included. The joke is the premise, not the build. A local-first PWA that keeps its data in the browser (IndexedDB); optional sync exists and is off by default.
imageAlt: Weekly Retro in present mode, showing slide 4 of an auto-assembled 12-slide review deck alongside the full slide rail. Demo data only.
